title: Corrected exp-38 retry: fixed illumination-invariant channel + from-scratch trunk + cross-lighting consistency loss, gate deleted
hypothesis: 20 straight rounds since champion (exp-35, 743.07 m) have swept nearly every decode/aggregation family (VQ codebook, continuous GMM, dense per-patch consensus under 3 different aggregators, spatial MoE, retrieve-rerank, factorized axes, coarse-to-fine) and every plausible trunk-objective swap (contrastive, joint/sequential reconstruction, ShuffleNetV2-pretrained, from-scratch x5) on top of the champion's field+soft-argmax decode, and all of them lost -- several catastrophically. The single closest post-champion result in the entire history is exp-42 (846.42 m, +14%), which is the ONE experiment that changed only the trunk's pretraining objective (contrastive) while leaving the champion's field/decode/rotation-ensemble shape untouched; every experiment that also rewrote the decode landed at 1100-2655 m or worse. That pattern says the decode family is not the wall -- the trunk's descriptor content is. But no trunk-objective swap tried so far has attacked the specific, previously-diagnosed nuisance in that descriptor: iter-12 probes (project memory champion-failure-mode-probes; also cited by exp-33/38) found the champion's descriptor rides low-level resampling-blur statistics that carry zero location information (removing rotation-resample blur nearly doubles error, 983->1668 m on a matched crop), and CLAUDE.md SS4 itself names the fix at the data-generation level: separate reflected AMBIENT light (dims with time-of-day) from ACTIVE artificial lighting (streetlamps/windows, lighting-invariant). Exp 38 proposed giving the trunk a fixed, non-learned Retinex-style illumination-invariant channel (log-luminance minus its own large-radius Gaussian blur) precisely to hand the network that decomposition explicitly instead of hoping fine-tuning discovers it -- but it was REJECTED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION, correctly, for leaving the lighting gate/field/confidence/training-signal stages self-reported unchanged under the pivot rule. The retinex idea itself was never trained or measured, unlike every learned-canonicalization alternative already tried and refuted (exp 43/44's reconstruction translators, exp 54's memory-safe corrected retry) -- this is a categorically different mechanism (a fixed geometric transform, not a learned translator with its own capacity/loss to fail), so it is not a repeat of those three refutations. This design is exp-38's corrected, fully-compliant re-attempt: every stage it touches actually changes in the code, and the fixed retinex channel is paired with a genuinely new training-signal addition (a cross-lighting descriptor-consistency loss) that gives the invariance hypothesis a second, independent lever rather than resting on the input channel alone. The champion's mobilenet_v3_small/mnv3s_features8.pt trunk is banned this round regardless, which forces a from-scratch trunk -- used here as the occasion to also delete the two-expert bright/dark gate (exp 12), since the retinex channel is meant to supply architecturally the invariance the gate was patching statistically.
method: In model/model.py: (1) delete the mobilenet_v3_small import and _build_pretrained_trunk/PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH/IMAGENET_MEAN/IMAGENET_STD -- replace with a new from-scratch compact conv trunk (~4-5 conv blocks reaching an 8x8 spatial output, channel count sized to keep the exported ONNX comfortably under the 4 MiB gate) whose first conv accepts 4 input channels. (2) Add a fixed, non-learned Retinex-style preprocessing step computed inside forward() from the raw [0,1] RGB input: luminance -> log1p -> large-radius Gaussian blur (fixed depthwise-conv buffer, no gradient, sigma on the order of ~16 px on the 128x128 crop) -> retinex = log-luminance minus its own blur, clamped/rescaled to roughly [0,1] -- concatenated as a 4th channel before the first learned conv layer. This is computed from the existing ONNX input, so the (1x3x128x128 float32 [0,1]) export contract is unchanged. (3) Delete the dark_logits/gate branch entirely -- a single loc_logits head reads the unified layout+GAP descriptor (same field/decode math: Gaussian-smoothed-CE-trained 32x32 grid, DECODE_BETA-sharpened soft-argmax, unchanged) built from the new trunk's output. (4) Confidence head is rebuilt to read the new (non-gated) field's shape statistics (peak mass, entropy, sharpened-vs-unsharpened gap) -- same mechanism as champion, wired to the new descriptor since the old gate-derived inputs no longer exist. (5) Add a `return_descriptor: bool` option to TinyLocNet.forward so train.py can retrieve the pooled post-rotation-average GAP descriptor for the consistency loss (mirrors the existing return_logits pattern). In model/train.py: (6) sample_epoch additionally draws, for each per-bucket batch, one 'lighting partner' crop per location at the identical (cx, cy, heading) but from one other uniformly-random bucket (reusing the already-cached per-bucket renders/realizations -- no new rendering cost), returned alongside the primary batch. (7) train_area's step loop forwards both the primary and partner crop batches (return_descriptor=True) and adds a new CONSISTENCY_WEIGHT-scaled L2 term between their pooled descriptors to the existing loss_fn output, backpropagated jointly. (8) Keep EPOCH_MULT, TRAIN_REALIZATIONS, CONFUSABILITY_ALPHA, and the calibration procedure exactly as champion -- do not also scale up training length, since the partner-view forward pass already roughly doubles per-step compute and four areas must still finish in sensible wall time.
expected_outcome: If the descriptor's blur/lighting-nuisance riding (not decode shape, not trunk-objective family per se) is the real remaining tax, this should beat exp-42's 846.42 m (the best post-champion result, achieved by a trunk-objective swap alone with no invariance mechanism) by a clear margin, landing roughly in the 650-900 m range -- plausibly at or below the champion's 743.07 m if the fixed retinex channel plus the consistency loss jointly buy back most of what going from-scratch costs. Mechanism-level signature to check post-hoc: the consistency loss term should converge to a visibly low value by the end of training (the same location's descriptor genuinely converging across lighting buckets, not just going to zero via representation collapse -- check that per-location descriptors still vary meaningfully ACROSS different locations); a rerun of the iter-12-style blur-ablation probe should show the crisp-vs-blurred-crop error gap (983 vs 1668 m in the historical probe) narrow measurably versus champion. Falsification forks: (a) if the metric lands near or below exp-42's 846 m with a healthy, non-collapsed consistency loss, the invariance hypothesis is supported and future rounds should keep exploring this channel (larger retinex radius, a learned but cheap fusion of RGB+retinex, or restoring a lighter dispatcher on top); (b) if the metric is flat/worse than exp-42 despite healthy training signals, the wall is not lighting-nuisance riding either, and after every named CLAUDE.md SS3 pivot family (dispatcher, quantization, coordinate reparameterization) plus this invariance attempt has failed, future rounds should treat raw training-data SCALE (more locations/epochs, not sampling weight) or accepting the current decode as near-optimal and focusing purely on calibration/coverage as the remaining levers; (c) if the consistency loss collapses to zero while the primary CE/coordinate loss stays high (representation collapse -- descriptors becoming lighting-invariant by becoming location-invariant too), CONSISTENCY_WEIGHT was set too high and the next attempt should retry at a smaller weight rather than abandoning the mechanism.
eli5: Every recent experiment has tried a different way for the model to guess a location, or a different pretrained starting brain for it, and all of them lost to the current champion. This time we try something the project noticed early but never actually got to test properly: give the model a second, cleaned-up version of the photo, computed by simple non-learned math, that strips out roughly how bright the whole scene is and keeps mostly the sharp edges and shapes -- like handing it a rough charcoal sketch alongside the color photo. Buildings and roads look the same in that sketch whether it's noon or midnight; only the color photo changes drastically. We also add a training rule that nudges the model's internal summary of 'what this place looks like' to stay the same whether the photo was rendered as daytime or nighttime, since it's the same physical spot either way.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px aerial crop, one of 6 simulated lighting conditions

stages.name: Illumination-invariant channel
stages.detail: a fixed, non-learned math transform (no training involved) computed from the raw photo: how bright each patch is compared to its own broad neighborhood average, which stays roughly the same across all 6 lighting conditions for the same physical spot -- stacked onto the raw color photo before anything else happens

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: a brand-new, never-pretrained small conv stack, trained from scratch, reading the color photo plus the new invariant sketch together

stages.name: Rotation fan
stages.detail: the crop and its four 90° turns still all travel through the same network side by side, but now the four turns' internal summaries are also nudged to agree with the summary from the SAME spot's photo taken under a different lighting condition, not just averaged together at the very end

stages.name: Location field
stages.detail: the old two-expert bright/dark blend is removed -- one unified scorer reads the new descriptor and produces the same kind of map-cell heat map as before, since the invariant channel is meant to do the job the two-expert split used to patch for

stages.name: Decode
stages.detail: unchanged mechanism: sharpen the heat map's contrast, then answer with its balance point

stages.name: Confidence
stages.detail: recomputed from the new unified heat map's shape (same recipe: crisp hotspot = sure, smear = unsure) since the old gate-derived inputs it used to read no longer exist

stages.name: Training data
stages.detail: each training batch now also loads, for the exact same spot and viewing angle, one extra photo under a different, randomly chosen lighting condition -- used only to teach the new consistency idea below

stages.name: Training procedure
stages.detail: one extra forward pass per batch (the same-spot, different-lighting photo); training length otherwise unchanged so four areas still finish in reasonable time

stages.name: Training signal
stages.detail: the usual grading (reward probability near the true spot) plus a new small penalty whenever the same spot's internal summary looks different between its two lighting versions

implementation_brief: Edit model/model.py: (A) Remove `from torchvision.models import mobilenet_v3_small`, `PRETRAINED_TRUNK_PATH`, `IMAGENET_MEAN`, `IMAGENET_STD`, and `_build_pretrained_trunk()`. Add `_build_trunk()` returning a from-scratch nn.Sequential of plain Conv2d+BatchNorm+ReLU blocks, input channels=4, downsampling (stride-2 blocks) until the 128x128 input reaches an 8x8 spatial output (mirrors the existing feat_ch/fmap_hw usage below -- keep channel counts modest, e.g. 32->64->96->128, so total params plus the field head stay well under the 4 MiB ONNX gate; verify with pipeline/score.py's actual export-size check, not just a param count estimate). (B) Add a registered non-trainable buffer for a fixed 2D Gaussian blur kernel (e.g. 31x31, sigma~4 px in normalized blur units matching a ~16 px effective radius on the 128x128 crop) and a method `_retinex_channel(self, x)`: `lum = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)`; `loglum = torch.log1p(lum * 255.0)`; blur it via `F.conv2d` with the fixed kernel (padding='same' / reflect pad, groups=1, no grad -- wrap in `torch.no_grad()` or ensure the buffer has `requires_grad=False`); `retinex = loglum - blurred`; normalize/clamp to roughly [0,1] (e.g. `(retinex.clamp(-3,3) + 3) / 6`). In `forward()`, build the 4-channel input as `torch.cat([x, retinex], dim=1)` BEFORE the existing `_c4_stack` call (so all 4 rotation copies get their own retinex channel computed consistently -- compute retinex once on `x` then rotate the 4-channel tensor, OR compute retinex per-rotated-copy; either is fine as long as it's deterministic and the ONNX input contract (`1x3x128x128` float32 `[0,1]`, RGB only) is unchanged -- the retinex channel must be derived INSIDE the model from the 3-channel input, never added to the exported input signature). (C) Delete `self.dark_logits` and `self.gate`; forward() should compute a single `logits4 = self.loc_logits(torch.cat([f4, layout4], dim=1))` (no gated blend) -- everything downstream (C4 logit averaging, sharpened/unsharpened decode, peak/entropy/gap confidence stats) stays structurally the same, just reading the new trunk's `feat_ch` (update `self.layout_squeeze`, `self.loc_logits`, `self.conf_head` input dims to match the new trunk's probe shape, same pattern as the existing `probe = self.features(...)` shape-inference code). (D) Add `return_descriptor: bool = False` param to `forward()`; when true, additionally return the post-rotation-averaged GAP descriptor `f` (already computed) as a third tuple element alongside `(out, logits)`. Preserve the existing `return_logits` behavior/signature exactly (only append, don't reorder). (E) Keep `loss_fn`'s existing CE + coordinate L2 + confidence BCE terms completely unchanged; do NOT add the consistency term inside loss_fn -- compute it in train.py instead (see below) and add it to the scalar returned by loss_fn before `.backward()`. Edit model/train.py: (F) In `sample_epoch`, after building `xs, ys` as today, also build a parallel `xs_partner` list: for every crop drawn in the primary loop (same `bucket`, same `i`/location, same `angle`, same realization index `r`), pick one `partner_bucket = rng.choice([b for b in LIGHTING_BUCKETS if b != bucket])` and extract the crop at the identical `(cx, cy, angle)` from that partner bucket's already-cached image (bucket-0 renders live at `area_dir(...)/'relight'/f'{bucket}.png'`, realizations r>=1 live in `renders_dir` -- reuse the same image-loading logic already in this function, just indexed by `partner_bucket` instead of `bucket`, loading each partner bucket's image at most once per epoch). Return `x, y, x_partner` (stack `xs_partner` the same way as `xs`). (G) Add `CONSISTENCY_WEIGHT = 0.1` (module constant, tune only if training logs show the consistency loss dominates or the primary CE loss stalls -- do not treat this as the experiment's free variable, keep it fixed and log it). (H) In `train_area`'s step loop, replace the existing `out, logits = model(xb, return_logits=True)` call with a single call requesting both flags (`out, logits, f_primary = model(xb, return_logits=True, return_descriptor=True)` -- do not add a separate third forward pass for the primary batch), forward the partner batch as `_, _, f_partner = model(xb_partner, return_logits=True, return_descriptor=True)`, compute `consistency_loss = ((f_primary - f_partner) ** 2).mean()`, and use `loss = loss_fn(out, logits, yb) + CONSISTENCY_WEIGHT * consistency_loss` for the backward pass. `xb_partner` is built from `x_partner` exactly like `xb` is built from `x` (same permute/div_/to(device) treatment, same `idx` slicing). (I) Log `consistency_weight` and `retinex_sigma` (or the kernel size used) in the `info` dict; change the `init` field to `"from-scratch (banned pretrained trunk this round); 4-channel input (RGB + fixed non-learned retinex-invariant channel)"`. Preserve exactly: train.py's CLI (`--area --out-dir --data-dir --epochs --max-crops-per-bucket --seed`), the ONNX export contract in model.py's docstring (1x3x128x128 float32 [0,1] input, [[u, v, conf]] output, opset 17), and `estimate_position()`'s signature -- none of these change.
